title: The HR helper that guessed
scenario:
You are an HR operations lead at a logistics company with 2,400 staff. The HR team tried a chat assistant for staff questions. It uses a general model with a short role prompt and no company documents.

The HR director says: "It sounds confident, but staff complain it is wrong. Should we buy a bigger model?" The exhibit shows the test log.
exhibit:
HR helper: test log (made-up example data)

Setup: general model, role prompt only, no company documents

#  Question                                  Assistant said        Handbook says        Result
1  Annual leave for new staff?               "Usually 20 days"     26 days              wrong
2  How much unused leave can I carry over?   "Most firms: 5 days"  10 days (changed     wrong
                                                                   in March 2026)
3  Rota-tool code for sick leave?            "Use SL"              AB-2                 wrong
4  Gross pay vs net pay?                     correct explanation   -                    right
5  Make my leave email more polite           good rewrite          -                    right

Score: 2 of 5

questions.prompt: What do the three wrong answers have in common?

options.text: Each one asks for an exact value, and the model is weak at giving exact values like these.
options.explanation: The model can give exact values it has seen. It can't know values it never saw. The pattern is missing company facts, not exact values.

options.text: Each one needs a polite tone, and the role prompt doesn't set the tone.
options.explanation: Tone was not the problem: the rewrite in test 5 was good. The wrong answers state wrong facts.

options.text: Each one needs company facts the model never saw: rules, a recent change, a code.
options.explanation: Right. These are the gaps OpenAI's accuracy guide lists for context work: private information and knowledge that is out of date.

options.text: Each one is too short for the model to understand what the staff member means.
options.explanation: Tests 4 and 5 were short too and went well. The model understood the questions; it lacked the facts.

questions.prompt: Which first fix fits OpenAI's accuracy guide best?

options.text: Add the current handbook to the context and tell the model to answer only from it.
options.explanation: Right. The failures are a context problem, so the fix is to supply the textbook. Anthropic's hallucination guide also suggests limiting answers to the provided documents.

options.text: Fine-tune the model on 2,000 past HR emails so that it learns the company rules.
options.explanation: The guide links fine-tuning to behaviour, such as tone and format. Old emails may also hold the leave rule from before March 2026.

options.text: Switch to the model with the latest knowledge cutoff and run the same five tests.
options.explanation: A newer cutoff doesn't add private facts like the 26-day rule or the AB-2 code. The context gap stays.

options.text: Add "Be accurate and check your facts" to the role prompt and run the tests again.
options.explanation: The model has no source to check against. An instruction can't supply facts that are not in the context.

questions.prompt: The team now plans to paste all 1,800 pages of HR files, including every old version since 2018, into each request. What is the best response?

options.text: Good plan. More context always gives the model more chances to find the answer.
options.explanation: Anthropic's context engineering post describes context rot: recall goes down as the context grows.

options.text: Good plan, as long as the old versions sit at the end of the prompt, after the new ones.
options.explanation: Order doesn't fix the real problem. Old versions give conflicting answers, such as 5 or 10 carry-over days.

options.text: Drop the files and wait for a model whose knowledge cutoff is after March 2026.
options.explanation: The 26-day rule and the AB-2 code are private. No public model learns them from its training data.

options.text: Send only the current, relevant pages, and test answers at different context sizes.
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic's post advises the smallest set of high-signal tokens, and OpenAI's guide says to evaluate long context at different sizes.

questions.prompt: The assistant invented the code "SL" in test 3. Which prompt change fits Anthropic's hallucination guide?

options.text: Add an "I don't know" rule; then invented answers stop, and checks can end.
options.explanation: The guide says these techniques reduce hallucinations but don't remove them. Critical answers still need checking.

options.text: Allow it to say "I don't know" when the handbook has no answer, and keep spot checks.
options.explanation: Right. The guide lists explicit permission to admit uncertainty, and it says to keep checking critical information.

options.text: Ask it to always give some answer, so staff are never left without help.
options.explanation: That pushes the model to guess. The guide recommends the opposite: permission to say "I don't know".

options.text: Ask it to sound less confident in every answer, so staff will double-check by themselves.
options.explanation: A less confident tone still gives the wrong code. The guide's step is to allow "I don't know", not to soften wrong answers.
